verdict.reasoning: Headache details match: left-sided, throbbing, since mid-day, worse with movement and leaning forward/head/neck movement: “on the left side… mid-day… it’s throbbing… if I lean forward, or like move my head or neck, yeah, headache gets worse.”

Patient reports visual aura with zig-zag lines and blurred vision in both eyes: “I noticed some zig-zag lines in my vision a few minutes before the headache started… My vision blurred… both eyes, OK.”

Photophobia and sunglasses use are explicitly mentioned: “Have you any difficulty with seeing bright lights, at all?” Patient: “Yeah well I'm, wearing sunglasses right now. It's just, you know, the light's really hurting my eyes.”
Nausea and two vomiting episodes are documented: “you mentioned that you felt quite nauseous. Have you vomited at all?” Patient: “Yeah… I vomited twice.”

Prior similar headache, duration, and response are stated: “I did have a similar headache a few weeks ago.”… “How long did it last for?” Patient: “Couple of days.”… “I had to take painkillers, and had to go to bed and rest.”
Patient denies being headache-prone: “Um, I'm not really prone to them, no.”

Denials of fever, rash, speech issues, limb symptoms, balance issues, and head injury are all present: “no I don't feel feverish”… “No, I haven't noticed anything like that [rash].”… “problems with your speech…?” Patient: “No.”… “problems with your arms and legs…?” Patient: “No.”… “difficulty with balance…?” Patient: “No.”… “Have you had a fall recently, or been knocked on the head?” Patient: “No.”
No past medical problems reported: “Do you have any other medical history I should be aware of?” Patient: “No, nothing.”
Medication, duration, and indication are stated: “Um I take the pill, Microgynon.”… “How long have you been on that for?” Patient: “three months.”… “it's for contraception.”
Family history includes migraines and underactive thyroid in mother: “My mum, my mum has, has migraines.”… “My mom has an underactive thyroid as well.”
Patient denies family history of brain cancer: “any other problems with for example, the brain, or? Um you mentioned brain cancer. Any other family history of ?” Patient: “No.”
Occupation, job stress, and living situation documented: “I work in the fashion industry… managers like putting a lot of pressure on me… it's not a good time.” and “I live on my own.”
No exercise, smoking, or alcohol use reported: “Do you do much in the way of exercise?” Patient: “No.”… “do you smoke at all? and do you drink much in the way of alcohol?” Patient: “No. No.”

Migraine with aura assessment is consistent with history and doctor’s impression: unilateral throbbing headache, visual aura, photophobia, nausea/vomiting, second similar episode, no focal neurological symptoms, afebrile by report. Doctor: “I wonder whether you may, may have a migraine… very classical… the headache on one side, throbbing nature, the nausea, vomiting, sensitivity to bright lights… this is the second migraine you've had in the space of a month… I’m reassured that you don't have anything more serious.”

Clear cancer-related health anxiety: patient repeatedly worries about brain cancer and tumor, referencing friend’s mother: “I've read… it could be a sign of brain cancer… what if it is a brain tumour? What's gonna happen with my future and my career?”
Analgesia plan matches: “some strong painkillers would be advisable. So, think about Paracetamol, or even Co-codamol. Um, and some anti-inflammatories, such as Ibuprofen and Naproxen.”
Headache diary advice is explicit: “keeping a headache diary would be quite important, to see exactly what's triggering these headaches.”

Follow-up and prophylaxis considered: “if your headaches were to become more persistent, then we could maybe think about giving you some medications that will stop your headaches from happening in the first place, something prophylactic medicines… we could have a discussion next time I see you next week, perhaps.”

Safety-netting instructions are explicitly given: “if your symptoms aren't getting better next two three days, or indeed they're getting worse… if your headache's getting worse, not responding to medications… Or your neck pain is getting worse, or you develop any weakness in your arms and legs, or your vision, then I want you to come back and see me straight away.”

Doctor reassures regarding meningitis and brain cancer: “I'm reassured that you don't have anything more serious, such as meningitis, or indeed Brain cancer, I know that was a big worry of yours initially.”
